MORTGAGE FORECLOSURE CONSULTANTS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield · Pat Morgan

PURPOSE AND SCOPE — INFORMATIONAL ONLY
This information sheet describes, in general terms, California's regulation of "foreclosure consultants" under the Mortgage Foreclosure Consultants article of the Civil Code, California Civil Code §§ 2945–2945.11. It concerns the residence commonly known as 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield, owned by Pat Morgan, and a person or business identified as Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC, located at 456 Business Ave, Suite 200, Sacramento, California, who has solicited or offered to perform, for compensation, one or more services described in this article in connection with that residence. This sheet summarizes, at a general level: who is and is not a "foreclosure consultant" as the statute defines that term; the legislative findings underlying the article; the written-contract and mandatory-notice content the statute requires; the owner's statutory right to cancel a foreclosure-consultant contract; the statute's advance-fee and loan-interest-rate limits; its bars on security interests, powers of attorney, and property-interest acquisitions by a foreclosure consultant; the private right of action and its limitations period; and the license/bonding disclosures required of certain representatives. It is distinct from — and does not duplicate — information sheets elsewhere in this corpus describing California's general nonjudicial foreclosure process under Civil Code § 2924 et seq., the Homeowner Bill of Rights servicer-conduct protections, and the Home Equity Sales Contract Act's separate regulation of "equity purchasers" who buy a residence in foreclosure outright; a foreclosure consultant, as defined here, provides services to an owner rather than purchasing the owner's property. This sheet is informational only. It does not itself form, cancel, or enforce any contract with Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC, determine whether Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC meets the statutory definition of a foreclosure consultant or any exemption from it, or determine whether any conduct toward Pat Morgan concerning 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield has complied — or failed to comply — with any statute described here.

LEGISLATIVE FINDINGS UNDERLYING THE FORECLOSURE CONSULTANT STATUTE
The article regulating foreclosure consultants opens with the Legislature's own statement of the problem it addresses. California Civil Code § 2945(a) states: "The Legislature finds and declares that homeowners whose residences are in foreclosure are subject to fraud, deception, harassment, and unfair dealing by foreclosure consultants from the time a Notice of Default is recorded pursuant to Section 2924 until the time surplus funds from any foreclosure sale are distributed to the homeowner or his or her successor." The same subdivision goes on to describe how such consultants "often charge high fees, the payment of which is often secured by a deed of trust on the residence to be saved, and perform no service or essentially a worthless service," and how vulnerable homeowners are sometimes induced to assign surplus foreclosure-sale proceeds to a consultant for a fee that a homeowner could otherwise recover directly from the trustee at minimal cost. Subdivision (c) directs that the article's provisions "shall be liberally construed" to effectuate its remedial purposes. Whether any dealings between Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC and Pat Morgan involving 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield match the pattern these findings describe is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The Legislature finds and declares that homeowners whose residences are in foreclosure are subject to fraud, deception, harassment, and unfair dealing by foreclosure consultants from the time a Notice of Default is recorded pursuant to Section 2924 until the time surplus funds from any foreclosure sale are distributed to the homeowner or his or her successor."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: This quotation states the Legislature's own findings as background to the operative rules that follow in this sheet's later clauses — it is not itself an operative rule imposing a duty or granting a right, and a court could decline to treat it as an independent source of liability separate from the specific operative subdivisions (§§ 2945.2 through 2945.11) it introduces. This is California statutory law, presented as evidence of one state's approach to regulating foreclosure-assistance services — not a claim about which state's law governs any particular consultant's conduct.

STATUTORY DEFINITION OF "FORECLOSURE CONSULTANT"
California Civil Code § 2945.1(a) defines the term this article regulates: "“Foreclosure consultant” means any person who makes any solicitation, representation, or offer to any owner to perform for compensation or who, for compensation, performs any service which the person in any manner represents will in any manner do any of the following:(1) Stop or postpone the foreclosure sale." The remainder of subdivision (a) lists eight further categories of represented service — among them obtaining forbearance, assisting with reinstatement or loan extensions, obtaining a loan or advance of funds, avoiding impairment of the owner's credit, "saving" the residence from foreclosure, and assisting the owner to obtain remaining sale proceeds — any one of which brings a paid solicitor or performer within the definition. Whether Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC's solicitations or services concerning 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield fall within this definition is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Foreclosure consultant” means any person who makes any solicitation, representation, or offer to any owner to perform for compensation or who, for compensation, performs any service which the person in any manner represents will in any manner do any of the following:(1) Stop or postpone the foreclosure sale."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.1(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.1(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.1.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: The definition is broad by design and reaches solicitation alone ("makes any solicitation, representation, or offer") even absent a completed contract; this sheet quotes only the introductory clause and its first enumerated category (stopping or postponing the foreclosure sale) rather than reproducing all nine enumerated categories in subdivision (a), so the quoted text is not the definition's complete substantive reach.

PERSONS THE DEFINITION EXCLUDES
California Civil Code § 2945.1(b) lists categories of persons who are not "foreclosure consultants" even if they perform services described in subdivision (a). It begins: "A foreclosure consultant does not include any of the following:(1) A person licensed to practice law in this state when the person renders service in the course of his or her practice as an attorney at law." Subdivision (b) continues through nine numbered exclusions, also covering persons licensed as prorater, real estate broker or salesperson acting under that license, licensed contractors, persons acting under express HUD or other government-agency authority, a lienholder servicing its own obligation, licensed consumer lenders, banks and similar regulated depository or title/escrow entities, and licensed residential mortgage lenders or servicers acting under that license. Subdivision (c) then narrows one of those exclusions: a person who arranges for payment of an owner's remaining foreclosure-sale surplus proceeds (the ninth category of service in subdivision (a)) is a foreclosure consultant "unless he or she is the owner's attorney," regardless of any other exemption. Whether Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC qualifies for any listed exclusion is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A foreclosure consultant does not include any of the following:(1) A person licensed to practice law in this state when the person renders service in the course of his or her practice as an attorney at law."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.1(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.1(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.1.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the attorney-practicing-law exclusion, the first of nine listed in subdivision (b); the other eight exclusions (summarized but not quoted here) carry their own conditions — for example, several apply only when the person is "acting under the authority of" a specified license, so licensure alone does not automatically exempt someone performing unrelated services. Subdivisions (b) and (c) of the same section are described together in this clause; they are not independent sources of each other.

OWNER'S STATUTORY RIGHT TO CANCEL A FORECLOSURE CONSULTANT CONTRACT
California Civil Code § 2945.2(a) gives an owner a statutory cancellation window independent of any other rescission right: "In addition to any other right under law to rescind a contract, an owner has the right to cancel such a contract until midnight of the fifth business day, as defined in subdivision (e) of Section 1689.5, after the day on which the owner signs a contract that complies with Section 2945.3." Under subdivisions (b) through (d), cancellation occurs when the owner gives written notice to the foreclosure consultant by mail, facsimile, or electronic mail at the address or number specified in the contract; mailed notice is effective on deposit in the mail, postage prepaid; and the notice need not use any particular form so long as it indicates the owner's intent not to be bound. Whether a contract between Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC and Pat Morgan complies with Civil Code § 2945.3 — the trigger for this cancellation window — or whether any cancellation right concerning that contract has been exercised or has expired, is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "In addition to any other right under law to rescind a contract, an owner has the right to cancel such a contract until midnight of the fifth business day, as defined in subdivision (e) of Section 1689.5, after the day on which the owner signs a contract that complies with Section 2945.3."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.2(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.2(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.2.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: The five-business-day period runs from the day the owner signs a contract that complies with Section 2945.3; a noncompliant contract does not necessarily start this clock in the same way, and Civil Code § 2945.3(h) (addressed separately, not quoted in this sheet) separately provides that an owner may cancel until the consultant has complied with the content requirements of Section 2945.3 at all. This sheet does not evaluate compliance with Section 2945.3 for any specific contract.

REQUIRED WRITTEN CONTRACT CONTENT AND STATUTORY WARNING NOTICE
California Civil Code § 2945.3(a) requires that any foreclosure-consultant contract take a specific written form: "Every contract shall be in writing and shall fully disclose the exact nature of the foreclosure consultant’s services and the total amount and terms of compensation." Subdivision (b) additionally requires a specific statutory warning to appear on the contract in large boldface type: "The following notice, printed in at least 14-point boldface type and completed with the name of the foreclosure consultant, shall be printed immediately above the statement required by subdivision (d):" As set out in the statute, that notice must state, in substance, that the named consultant cannot take or ask for money until everything promised has been completely finished, and cannot ask the owner to sign any lien, deed of trust, or deed. Subdivisions (c) through (g) add further requirements: the contract must be in the language principally used to negotiate it (with a translated copy available on request in specified circumstances); it must be dated, signed, and carry a boldface right-to-cancel statement near the owner's signature; it must list the consultant's contact information and the signing date on its first page; and it must be accompanied by a duplicate, easily detachable "Notice of Cancellation" form. Whether any contract concerning 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield satisfies these requirements is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every contract shall be in writing and shall fully disclose the exact nature of the foreclosure consultant’s services and the total amount and terms of compensation."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.3(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.3(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.3.&lawCode=CIV)
  "The following notice, printed in at least 14-point boldface type and completed with the name of the foreclosure consultant, shall be printed immediately above the statement required by subdivision (d):"
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.3(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.3(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.3.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: Both quoted passages are drawn from the same statutory section, Civil Code § 2945.3, subdivisions (a) and (b) — they are quoted together, rather than as independent sources, because subdivision (b)'s notice requirement is one of several form requirements subdivision (a) generally imposes. The full statutory notice text embeds contract-specific fill-in blanks (for the consultant's name) that do not render as continuous prose once extracted from the statute's HTML formatting; this sheet quotes only the clean introductory sentence describing where and how the notice must be printed, not the fill-in notice language itself, so the exact wording a compliant contract must display is not reproduced here.

PROHIBITION ON ADVANCE COMPENSATION AND CAP ON LOAN FEES/INTEREST
California Civil Code § 2945.4 opens by declaring certain conduct a violation for a foreclosure consultant, beginning with subdivision (a): a consultant may not "Claim, demand, charge, collect, or receive any compensation until after the foreclosure consultant has fully performed each and every service the foreclosure consultant contracted to perform or represented that he or she would perform." Subdivision (b) separately bars a consultant from charging excessive amounts on any loan the consultant itself makes to the owner: a consultant may not "Claim, demand, charge, collect, or receive any fee, interest, or any other compensation for any reason which exceeds 10 percent per annum of the amount of any loan which the foreclosure consultant may make to the owner." Whether any compensation sought or received by Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC from Pat Morgan in connection with 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield complies with either limitation is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Claim, demand, charge, collect, or receive any compensation until after the foreclosure consultant has fully performed each and every service the foreclosure consultant contracted to perform or represented that he or she would perform."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.4(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.4(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.4.&lawCode=CIV)
  "Claim, demand, charge, collect, or receive any fee, interest, or any other compensation for any reason which exceeds 10 percent per annum of the amount of any loan which the foreclosure consultant may make to the owner."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.4(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.4(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.4.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: Subdivisions (a) and (b) of Civil Code § 2945.4 are quoted together in this clause as related but textually distinct prohibitions within the same section — they are not independent sources of each other. Civil Code § 2945.6(a) (addressed in this sheet's remedies clause) ties a mandatory treble-damages remedy specifically to violations of subdivisions (a), (b), and (d) of this section, so the practical stakes of a subdivision (a) or (b) violation are addressed only partially by this clause standing alone.

BARS ON SECURITY INTERESTS, POWERS OF ATTORNEY, AND ACQUIRING AN INTEREST IN THE RESIDENCE
California Civil Code § 2945.4 further prohibits a foreclosure consultant from securing its compensation against the owner's property. Subdivision (c) bars a consultant from taking "Take any wage assignment, any lien of any type on real or personal property, or other security to secure the payment of compensation. That security shall be void and unenforceable." Subdivision (e) separately bars a consultant from acquiring an ownership interest in the residence from an owner it has contracted with: a consultant may not "Acquire any interest in a residence in foreclosure from an owner with whom the foreclosure consultant has contracted. Any interest acquired in violation of this subdivision shall be voidable, provided that nothing herein shall affect or defeat the title of a bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value and without notice of a violation of this article." The same subdivision states that this bar does not affect a bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value without notice, and that mere knowledge the property was in foreclosure does not itself constitute notice of a violation. Subdivision (f) separately bars a consultant from taking "Take any power of attorney from an owner for any purpose." Whether Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC has sought or obtained any security interest, power of attorney, or ownership interest concerning 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield from Pat Morgan is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Take any wage assignment, any lien of any type on real or personal property, or other security to secure the payment of compensation. That security shall be void and unenforceable."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.4(c) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.4(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.4.&lawCode=CIV)
  "Acquire any interest in a residence in foreclosure from an owner with whom the foreclosure consultant has contracted. Any interest acquired in violation of this subdivision shall be voidable, provided that nothing herein shall affect or defeat the title of a bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value and without notice of a violation of this article."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.4(e) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.4(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.4.&lawCode=CIV)
  "Take any power of attorney from an owner for any purpose."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.4(f) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.4(f) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.4.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: Subdivisions (c), (e), and (f) of Civil Code § 2945.4 are quoted together in this clause as related but textually distinct prohibitions within the same section — they are not independent sources of each other. Subdivision (e)'s voidability rule and its bona-fide-purchaser carve-out are fact-intensive; this sheet does not determine whether any particular transfer or purchaser would qualify for that carve-out.

PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION, DAMAGES, AND THE LIMITATIONS PERIOD
California Civil Code § 2945.6(a) gives an owner a private right of action for a violation of the article: "An owner may bring an action against a foreclosure consultant for any violation of this chapter. Judgment shall be entered for actual damages, reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs, and appropriate equitable relief." The same subdivision requires the court to award exemplary damages equal to at least three times the compensation the consultant received for violations of subdivision (a), (b), or (d) of Section 2945.4, and three times the owner's actual damages for violations of subdivision (c), (e), or (g) of that section, in addition to any other damages award; for other violations the court may, in its discretion, award exemplary damages. Subdivision (b) sets the time limit for bringing such an action: "Any action brought pursuant to this section shall be commenced within four years from the date of the alleged violation." Whether Pat Morgan has, or has timely exercised, any claim under this section concerning Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An owner may bring an action against a foreclosure consultant for any violation of this chapter. Judgment shall be entered for actual damages, reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs, and appropriate equitable relief."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.6(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.6(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.6.&lawCode=CIV)
  "Any action brought pursuant to this section shall be commenced within four years from the date of the alleged violation."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.6(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.6(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.6.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: Subdivisions (a) and (b) of Civil Code § 2945.6 are quoted together in this clause — they are not independent sources of each other. Subdivision (a)'s mandatory treble-damages rule cross-references particular subdivisions of a different section (Civil Code § 2945.4, addressed in two other clauses of this sheet); this clause does not itself determine whether any specific conduct falls within those cross-referenced subdivisions, and the remedies described here are cumulative to, not a limitation of, other rights and remedies available under other law.

LICENSE AND BOND DISCLOSURE REQUIRED OF CERTAIN REPRESENTATIVES
California Civil Code § 2945.11(a) imposes additional requirements on a specific category of representative acting for a foreclosure consultant (one meeting the definition cross-referenced in Civil Code § 2945.9(b)). Before any interest in the property transfers, such a representative must provide "Written proof to the owner that the representative has a valid current California Real Estate Sales License and that the representative is bonded by an admitted surety insurer in an amount equal to at least twice the fair market value of the real property that is the subject of the contract." Subdivision (a) also requires a written statement, under penalty of perjury, attesting to the same license and bond and to compliance with the written-proof requirement, delivered to all parties to the contract before any transfer of an interest in the property. Subdivision (b) provides that failure to comply renders the contract voidable at the owner's option and makes the foreclosure consultant liable for resulting damages. Whether this representative-specific requirement applies to any particular person acting for Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC in connection with 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield is not addressed by this sheet.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Written proof to the owner that the representative has a valid current California Real Estate Sales License and that the representative is bonded by an admitted surety insurer in an amount equal to at least twice the fair market value of the real property that is the subject of the contract."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 2945.11(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 2945.11(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2945.11.&lawCode=CIV)
  Known gap: This requirement, by its terms, applies only to a "representative" as defined by cross-reference to Civil Code § 2945.9(b) — a section this sheet has not independently fetched or quoted — not to every foreclosure consultant or every person who deals with an owner; this sheet does not determine who qualifies as such a representative in any given transaction.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT — INFORMATIONAL SHEET ONLY
I have reviewed this information sheet describing California's regulation of foreclosure consultants under Civil Code §§ 2945–2945.11, including its application to dealings between Pat Morgan and Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC concerning the residence at 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield. I understand that this document is informational only: it does not itself form, cancel, or enforce any contract; determine whether Sunrise Foreclosure Solutions LLC meets the statutory definition of a foreclosure consultant or qualifies for any statutory exemption; evaluate any specific contract's compliance with the written-form, notice, or cancellation-window requirements described in this sheet; calculate any fee, interest, or damages amount; or otherwise resolve whether any actual conduct toward Pat Morgan or 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield has complied — or failed to comply — with the statutes described here. I further understand that this sheet is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney about any specific contract, dispute, or transaction.

Executed on September 1, 2026 at Oakland, California.
